techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse the Windows command shell for execution.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may use obfuscated files or information to hide artifacts of an intrusion.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login information.

techniques.name: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to access credential material stored in LSASS process memory.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries may inject code into processes to evade defenses and elevate privileges.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse BITS jobs to download, execute, and clean up after malicious code.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries may bypass process and/or signature-based defenses by proxying execution.

techniques.name: Mshta
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse mshta.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Regsvr32
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Regsvr32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Rundll32
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse rundll32.exe to proxy execution of malicious code.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse WMI to execute malicious commands and payloads.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse task scheduling functionality to facilitate execution.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Windows Task Scheduler to perform task scheduling for execution.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may delete or remove built-in OS data designed to aid in recovery.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: Adversaries may search for common password storage locations.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of accounts on a system or domain.

techniques.name: Domain Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.

techniques.name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to subvert Kerberos authentication.

techniques.name: System Services
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse system services to execute commands or programs.

techniques.name: Service Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Windows service control manager to execute malicious commands.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries may use remote services to access and persist within a network.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries may use SMB to interact with network shares for lateral movement.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries may configure system settings to automatically execute a program during boot or logon.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adversaries may achieve persistence by adding a program to startup folder or registry run key.

techniques.name: Winlogon Helper DLL
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Winlogon features to execute DLLs during logon.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal
techniques.description: Adversaries may delete or modify artifacts generated within systems to remove evidence.

techniques.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Adversaries may clear Windows Event Logs to hide activity.

techniques.name: Timestomp
techniques.description: Adversaries may modify file timestamps to hide malware or tools.

techniques.name: Hide Artifacts
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to hide artifacts associated with their behaviors.

techniques.name: Hidden Files and Directories
techniques.description: Adversaries may hide files by setting the hidden attribute.

techniques.name: NTFS File Attributes
techniques.description: Adversaries may use NTFS file attributes to hide malicious data.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability.
